The codeFlow shows the filename originates from line 235 (parameter input) and flows directly to line 266 (open call).

evidence.notes: This is a classic path traversal vulnerability where user input is used directly in file operations without validation. An attacker could craft S3 keys or filenames with path traversal sequences to access arbitrary files on the system.

findings.description: Multiprocessing Queue instantiation flagged as unsafe pickle usage - False Positive
findings.reasoning: This line creates a multiprocessing.Queue object with a size parameter. While multiprocessing.Queue uses pickle for serialization by default, this is NOT a deserialization vulnerability because: (1) The queue is used for inter-process communication within the same application, (2) Only internally-created objects (DownloadFileRequest, GetObjectJob) are put into the queue, (3) There is no untrusted/external data being deserialized, (4) The application controls all data flowing through these queues. CWE-502 (Deserialization of Untrusted Data) requires untrusted data as input, which is not present here. This is a false positive from the CodeQL query which flags all multiprocessing.Queue usage without considering the data source.
